scope: A1 Query-Aware Retrieval — final quality-economics Pareto analysis and frozen A1 decision

economics.cost_note: USD figures are uncached-equivalent estimates; cross-arm physical dedup must not be read as an independent-deployment cost for any arm.

economics_notes: rewrite_calls = 0 for every arm (frozen single-turn replay).

Only no_router_adaptive_v1 carries live per-call latency (it had no reusable answers); the other four arms READ cached generations and have no per-call latency, so latency is not treated as 0 and is not used for fair pairwise latency comparison.
provider total tokens/query is the primary architecture economics measure; evidence tokens and $/query are secondary.
dominance_rule: A strictly dominates B iff A is not worse on primary quality (QueryRequiredComplete, required covered/missing), has no more confirmed regressions, no worse correctness/grounding, and strictly lower provider tokens/query.

dominance_matrix.detail: worse on regressions, grounding and tokens

dominance_matrix_note: coverage_selector_v2 -> query_router_v1 is the only strict dominance relation among the five arms. All other pairs are quality-cost trade-offs (Pareto non-dominated).

material_benefit_vs_fixed.detail: gained 1 (VAL-001-006-F02, completing that case) but lost 1 (VAL-001-001-F03); contract requires zero lost aspects. Extra ~29.5% tokens buy no net required coverage.
gained 7, lost 3 (2 confirmed complete-regressions); not a zero-loss gain.
gained 8, lost 2 (1 confirmed complete-regression); not a zero-loss gain, at ~2.44x tokens.
gained 2, lost 2 (1 confirmed complete-regression); not a zero-loss gain.

router_decision.frozen_rule: query_aware_arms_v1.json: A1_ROUTER must beat no-router adaptive on quality-cost Pareto, otherwise delete router; economics_contract_v1.md complexity deletion when a simpler competitor ties on confirmed quality at equal or lower tokens.
evidence: query_router_v1 is strictly dominated by coverage_selector_v2 on every axis: equal QueryRequiredComplete (44/50), equal required covered (196), fewer confirmed regressions (0 vs 1), fewer correctness/grounding issues (1 vs 2), lower tokens/query (3281.1 vs 3667.7), lower $/query (0.00064523 vs 0.00069980), lower evidence tokens (125648 vs 143319).
coverage_selector_v2 uses no query classification, so the SIMPLE/BROAD signal adds no quality and only adds cost.

query_router_v1 also does not beat no_router_adaptive_v1 (worse quality and more grounding issues at lower cost is a trade-off, not a beat) and shows no material benefit vs fixed_top5 (gained 2, lost 2).
No router tuning is performed; the negative result is the formal A1 result.

a1_hypothesis_statement: SIMPLE/BROAD query classification gives query_router_v1 enough extra information to beat simpler query-classification-free strategies on quality-cost Pareto.
mechanism_interpretation: Query classification produced no unique answer-quality gain: the router ties selector and fixed on required coverage and QueryRequiredComplete while adding SIMPLE/BROAD machinery.
Evidence-side selection already captures enough allocation signal: coverage_selector_v2 matches the router's quality with fewer regressions, less cost, and no query classification.
The extra context routed to BROAD queries did not convert into required-aspect quality; the router is the only strictly dominated arm.

Scope limit: this conclusion holds only for the GitHub Policy benchmark, the frozen SIMPLE/BROAD rule, the frozen context policies, and the current model/retrieval setup. It does not generalize to 'query routing is always useless'.

surviving_architecture.rationale: Simplest and cheapest non-dominated strategy (2533.1 tokens/query), zero confirmed complete-regressions; no more-complex component delivers a material benefit (zero-loss gained aspect) justifying its added cost under the frozen complexity-deletion rule.
surviving_architecture.quality_ceiling_rationale: Non-dominated quality extreme (202/208 required covered, 46/50 complete) but ~2.44x tokens and 1 confirmed regression, so it is retained only as a reference ceiling, not the default.
surviving_architecture.role_note: Default (fixed_top5) and quality ceiling (no_router_adaptive_v1) are different roles; the ceiling is not the default.

a2_trigger.frozen_condition: A2 starts only on a human-confirmed BROAD multi-requirement failure with evidence the cause is original-query representation rather than context budget/selection.
a2_trigger.reason: A1 aggregate required-aspect data (e.g. no_router_adaptive_v1 still misses 6 aspects across 4 incomplete cases) is insufficient to attribute residual misses to representation versus context budget/selection. No failure-type decomposition was part of A1, so the trigger cannot be decided from the current aggregates.

caveats: Latency cannot be compared fairly across arms: only no_router_adaptive_v1 has live timers; the other four reused cached answers.
USD cost per query is an uncached-equivalent estimate; physical experiment dedup lowered the actual experiment bill and must not be read as an independent-deployment cost.
Grounding/citation diagnostics are secondary and judge-derived except where human-resolved (one human-confirmed contradicted claim on no_router_adaptive_v1 / VAL-001-046).
A1 used 50 Validation V1 cases; the 16 Broad Query V3 cases were not part of this answer-level comparison.
No composite quality score was constructed; multi-metric Pareto comparison only.
